born.why: The code prioritizes survival by eating immediately when starving (>90), avoids poisonous fruits based on history, and cautiously tastes unknown fruits only when hunger is low enough to survive a potential poisoning event, balancing knowledge acquisition with immediate caloric needs.

The code prioritizes survival by eating immediately when near death, avoids known poisonous fruits, and uses a safer threshold for tasting unknowns to prevent learning from fatal errors, while also distinguishing between carrying state decisions to optimize pantry delivery.

The code prioritizes survival by avoiding known poisons, eating known good fruits immediately when hungry, and carefully sampling unknown fruits only when hunger is low enough to survive a potential negative outcome, thus balancing exploration with safety.

The code prioritizes safety by avoiding known poisonous fruits, expands knowledge by tasting unknowns when not starving, and switches to blind eating only when starvation risk outweighs poisoning risk, ensuring long-term survival through learning while managing immediate hunger needs.

The code improves survival by using trait-based generalization to avoid poisonous fruits even if the species is new, adds a safety margin to prevent tasting when hunger is too high to risk poisoning, and prioritizes eating known-good fruits or emergency eating when starving.

The code prioritizes starvation survival, then distinguishes between known-safe foods (eat immediately), known-poisonous foods (leave), and unknowns (taste if not starving to expand knowledge, otherwise leave to conserve energy). It avoids eating unknowns when hungry because the risk of poisoning is too high compared to the benefit of a single taste, preferring to seek out known goods instead.
